content:
The test image shows soybean leaves with prominent interveinal chlorosis and necrosis - yellow/brown patches between veins while veins appear to remain green. This is a **leaf** disease.

Top candidates based on symptoms: Sudden_death_syndrome, Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus, Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus, Downy_mildew, Brown_Stem_Rot, Cercospora, Bacterial_Blight, Septoria_brown_spot.

Let me view one reference from each top candidate.
SDS reference shows very similar interveinal necrosis pattern with green veins. Strong match. Let me check other candidates.
SVN virus shows scattered small spots along veins - much less extensive than the test image. Not a match.
BPMV shows green-yellow mottling with puckering - different pattern from the test image (no necrosis). Not a match.
BSR shows very similar interveinal necrosis with green veins remaining - also a strong candidate. The pattern is quite similar to both SDS and the test image, though more advanced/dried out here.
Downy mildew shows small scattered yellow spots - very different pattern from the test image. Not a match.
Cercospora shows reddish-purple spots scattered across the leaf - different from the interveinal necrosis pattern in the test image. Not a match.

Bacterial blight shows small angular water-soaked/yellow spots - very different from the extensive interveinal necrosis in the test image. Not a match.

Now let me use my last view to compare SDS more closely, since SDS and BSR are my top two candidates. The key differentiator: SDS has white pith, BSR has brown pith (internal stem). But visually on leaves, both show interveinal necrosis. The test image shows leaves still on the plant with the classic "green veins, brown/yellow between" pattern. Let me view another SDS reference.

This confirms the SDS pattern. Both SDS references show the hallmark interveinal chlorosis/necrosis with green veins remaining clearly visible, which matches the test image very well.

**Analysis summary:**
- The test image shows extensive interveinal chlorosis and necrosis on soybean leaves, with veins remaining green.
- SDS reference images (views 1 and 8) show the same distinctive pattern: yellow spots between veins that expand to large chlorotic/necrotic blotches while midvein and lateral veins stay green.
- BSR (view 4) can look similar but was more uniformly brown/dried; the test image has more yellow-green mottling characteristic of SDS.
- All other candidates (SVN virus, BPMV, Downy mildew, Cercospora, Bacterial blight) showed distinctly different patterns.
- The KB description for SDS states "scattered yellow spots between leaf veins... grow to form large chlorotic and necrotic blotches between the leaf veins, while the midvein and major lateral veins remain green" - this is exactly what the test image shows.

Ruled out BSR (more uniformly dried brown), Cercospora (purple spots), Downy mildew (small scattered spots), Bacterial blight (angular spots), BPMV (mottling without necrosis), and SVN virus (spots along veins)."}
